Comments: Follow up inspection of the County of Cambria Yahner 4 well conducted on 09/22/2022. Arrived on location at 9:31. Violations were issued as a result of a 03/23/2022 site inspection (Inspection Record 3336666) for the following: OGA3220(A) - Failure to plug an abandoned well. 78.91(a) - Failure to plug an abandoned well. 78.103 - Failure to monitor well granted Inactive Status on an annual basis and submit monitoring reports. 78.104 - Failure to meet the terms of Inactive Status. 78.88(a) - Failure to inspect each well for compliance with requirements. 78.88(b)1-4 - Failure to meet minimum requirements for inspections. 78.88(e) - Failure to submit Mechanical Integrity Report to the Department. OGA3211(G) - Failure to post the permit number and operators info at the well site. OGA3211(H) - Failure to install the permit number on the well upon completion in a permanent manner. These concerns were also addressed in an email from the Department that was sent to the operator as a result of a 3/30/2021 site inspection (Inspection Record 3169309). A response from the operator was requested by the Department to discuss issues on site. No corrective actions were taken by the operator. This 9/22/2022 follow up inspection found that the well remains in a similar condition as the previous inspections. Violations were not addressed or responded to. Well is not equipped for production. Pumpjack remains on site, much of which is now dismantled. Meter and electric boxes remain on site. Does not appear to be connected to pipeline. No permit number or operator ID found on the well. Well status was previously approved as Regulatory Inactive. Regulatory Inactive status expired on 04/15/2020. Operator failed to plug or return the well to active status. Review found no annual integrity monitoring reports submitted to the Department. All of the above violations remain outstanding.

properties.content:

Violation ID: 8277688
Permit API: 003-22171
Unconventional: No
County: Allegheny
Municipality: Ohio Township
Inspection Type: Compliance Schedule Evaluation
Inspection Date: 6/08/2026
Comments: The Department conducted a compliance schedule evaluation of this well on 06/08/2026. Per an Order (No. 55 M.D. 2024) issued on March 27, 2025, the Operator of this well was required to plug the well by 6/30/2025. In addition to the plugging requirement, the Operator was required to... 1. Provide the Department with a schedule to complete plugging of the well. 2. Submit a fully completed Form 8000-FM-OG0005, "Notice of Intention by Well Operator to Plug a Well," and a well location plat for the wells to the Department not less than 3 and not more than 15 days before the plugging of each well. The Operator has failed to plug the well by the date indicated in the Order, and the Department has received no correspondence from the Operator indicating their intent to plug this well. The site is not prepped for plugging, and no equipment or personnel were on site that would indicate an intent to plug the well in the near future. The violation of OGA3259(1) remains outstanding. Note: The well continues to leak gas (Photo 2).

Unconventional: Yes

Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 10/04/2023
Comments: A follow-up inspection was conducted after the operator reported a release of produced fluid to the surface of Pad A from GPU #3 on 9/18/23. An area between GPU #3 and the southwest pad edge has been excavated including in the stormwater channel at the pad edge. Some fluid was present in the channel which had an electrical conductivity (EC) of 910 uS/cm. On Pad A, an area of secondary containment has been set up for the excavated pad material. The material has been tarped. The containment appears to be in good condition.Six wells are staged for production on Pad A. Six GPUs are present and appear to be in good condition.On Pad B, nine wells are staged for production. Nine GPUs are present within secondary containment. The GPUs and containment appear to be in good condition. Multiple batteries of frac tanks are present on the pad within secondary containment. A few puddles of fluid are present on the pad surface in front of the frac tank batteries which had an EC between 2.40 to 2.50 mS/cm. The Department recommends vacuuming up the fluid. The EC of the fluid in the sump at the east end of the north stormwater channel has an EC of 1645 uS/cm.Along the access road, vegetation has germinated where excavation took place after a truck rollover caused a release of produced fluid to an area surrounding the access road. The area is not yet permanently stabilized. Violations remain outstanding against permit 081-21855 for release of produced fluid to the surface of Pad A from 9/18/23.Violations remain outstanding for the release to Pad B from 2/21/23.

Comments: On August 27, 2025, the Department met on-site with the Operator and Moody and Associates to assess the access road culvert inlet. Accompanying me today is Lisa Raffle (Diversified), Glenn Wilson (Diversified), Jessie Bobrzynski (Moody), and Jona Stoskey (Moody).Due to the approximate specific conductivity threshold of 4.00 mS (according to Moody and Associates), the stained area observed in IR 4040776 on the access road will not be assessed. During today's on-site inspection/meeting, specific conductivity of the soil under the rip rap of the access road's culvert inlet was measured by the Department and Moody. Moody utilized their own specific conductivity probe/meter as well as a probe/meter supplied by Diversified. The Department utilized its own specific conductivity probe/meter. All three specific conductivity probes/meters were calibrated on-site prior to the inspection/meeting.Upon arrival to the culvert inlet, Lisa Raffle of Diversified informed the Department that she took readings of specific conductivity following the Department's latest on-site inspection (IR 4040776), to which she did not observe readings anywhere near as high as the Department did. The Department asked Raffle where the readings were taken from, to which Raffle indicated it was from the excavated area (Photo 2) within the culvert ditch. This small excavated area is observed to be upslope of the culvert and just downslope of the access road. The Department clarified that each of the specific conductivity readings for this inlet that were probed by the Department in previous on-site inspection were probed directly in front of the culvert inlet.Specific conductivity readings were probed by Moody and the Department in front of, under, and on the sides of the culvert inlet. Readings were observed to be 'Or' (Out of Range) or above 20.0 mS underneath and to the right (South) of the culvert. Glenn Wilson (Diversified) promptly removed approximately one and a half 5-gallon buckets of impacted material from this area (Photo 3).Following the removal of this material, Moody probed again and recorded readings between 6.0-10.0 mS underneath the culvert inlet. At this time, Diversified and Moody jointly decided to halt removal of material and collect a soil sample of the soil that was producing the 6.0-10.0 mS readings. The Department also collected a soil sample (SAC 960) from this location following Moody's collection. Based on today's inspection, all issued violations remain outstanding.

Unconventional: Yes

Comments: On December 15, 2023, I conducted an inspection of the WL Hopkins Well Site. The inspection was conducted in response to a request made by an PA DEP OGI during an inspection conducted on 12/15/2023 (Sub-SAIR# 3660126). At the time of inspection, the following was observed:Act 9 Sign Installed, however the Operator of Record does not appear to be correct. The associated PPC plan and ER plan on site have not been updated to reflect the change in ownership. (Photo 11 and 12)The COASTAL Drill Rig was on site and connected to the well. The drill rig and associated equipment was not placed within secondary containment. (Photo 1)I observed fluid on the well pad surrounding the WL Hopkins 590312 Well and drill rig. I also observed fluid within the well cellar. I collected conductivity readings of the fluid on the well pad and within the cellar, which result in elevated conductivity readings. I also observed what appeared to be a light colored crystallin substance deposited on the well pad rock adjacent to the standing fluid. The crystallin substance appears to be salt which suggest that the fluid has been on site long enough to begin evaporation. The amount of fluid on the well pad appeared to be greater than 42 gallons. At the time of inspection, the Department was not previously notified by the Operator of a release of fluid to the well pad. (Photo 2 thru 10)While I was on site, I contacted Operator representative Kevin Wright (CONSOL/Leatherwood) to relay my observations related to the fluid release and recommend that the Operator being remediation immediately. Mr. Wright indicated that the Operator added brine to the well to kill the well on 11/15/2023.I am requesting clarification of the activity, date and time of when the fluid was added to the well bore and all information/inspections related to the monitoring of the well between 11/15/2023 and 12/15/2023. I am also requesting clarification of the source of the fluid added to the well bore on or around 11/15/2023.Violation are being issued for the release (78a.54, 78a57(a), 91.34(a), SWMA 301, 78a66(b)1,78a(b)1(i), 78a66(b)1(ii), 78a66(b)(2), 91.33(a) and 91.33(b).Violations are being issued for the failure to develop a site specific PPC plan and ER Plan. 78a55(a), 78a55(b), 78a55(c). 78a55(h).Violations are being issued for the failure to properly update the Act 9 Sign (78a55(i)(4)(D)(III).Violations are being issued for the failure to install secondary containment. (78a64(a))

Violation ID: 871737
Permit API: 059-24428
Unconventional: Yes

Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 2019-12-20
Comments: The Department conducted an inspection of the Burchianti 11A gas well and production equipment on 12/20/2019. Diversified personnel are on location at the time of the inspection. The Department was notified by PEMA on 12/20/2019 of a loud explosion associated with the Burchianti 11A gas well. At the time of the inspection, the Burchianti 11A gas well is shut in. The operator shut in the well at approximately 2330 on 12/19/2019 in response to a production equipment failure. According to the operator, a failure of the production equipment caused explosive damage to the production equipment and a release of gas from the well. The gas release occurred from 2210 - 2330 on 12/19/2019 until the well was shut in by the operator at 2330 on 12/19/2109. The well is located approximately 300 feet north the production equipment and production tanks. No damage to the well was observed. At the location of the production equipment the Department observed damaged pieces of production equipment. The Department observed some gray black stained gravel at the former location of the separator. The gravel appears to be damp. Damage to the production unit is severe. Diversified personnel are searching the wooded area around the well site for additional pieces of the production equipment. The Department observed pieces of equipment being recovered approximately 70 feet from the source of the failure. Search and recovery of damaged equipment continued while the Department was on site. Two production tanks are located within an earthen containment adjacent to the location of the explosion. The Department observed small holes in the south side of the southern most tank. The north tank in the containment is severely corroded. A large severely corroded hole was observed on the southwest side upper portion of the tank. The hole is approximately 3' x 5'. The Department did not detect any combustible levels of gas during the inspection. In response to the incident, Diversified reported that surrounding wells have been shut in.

Comments: The Pennsylvania Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) conducted a follow-up inspection at Repsol's Broadleaf Holdings (01-115) well site located in Troy, Columbia and Springfield Townships, Bradford County on 8/20/2025 at 0830 hours. The weather was 62 degrees F with rain. The inspection was conducted to assess ongoing remedial activities after a well control incident on 7/13/2025 resulted in a produced fluids release.No remediation excavation activities were occurring today due to the rain. Impacted materials stored within secondary containment (photo #2) continue to be loaded into trucks and hauled offsite for disposal. An interceptor trench was installed around the entire secondary containment on the pad surface that collects fluids and diverts them into a pipe (photo #1) that eventually flows into the trench below the pad's fill slope. Fluids were flowing into the lined detention basin from both the eastern and western lined channels today (photos #5 and 6). Fluids flowing in the western channel were field measured at ~6mS/cm and fluids flowing the in the eastern channel were field measured at ~370us/cm. Less than 6 inches of fluids were currently held in the lined detention basin (photo #4).Resource Environmental collected samples from the three shallow, monitoring wells drilled downslope of the well pad on 8/7/2025. Repsol reported that the samples collected on 8/7/2025 from Monitoring Well (MW) MW04A showed that elevated constituents were reported. MW04A can be seen in photo #10 and is located downslope of the preexisting stormwater basin. During remediation of the preexisting stormwater basin, a large rock was removed and a ~4-inch borehole was discovered beneath the basin (photo #9). Repsol reported that the borehole was ~27 feet deep and was not discovered during construction because it is located on the fill side of the basin and was ~3 feet beneath the native soils. It is unclear at this time if the borehole is causing the elevated constituents found in MW04A. Resource Environmental continues weekly sampling from the three shallow, monitoring wells, streams and various seeps on the fill slope. Repsol intends to have confirmatory samples collected from the soils in the remediated stormwater basin, and then backfill, however, a permanent structure will be installed to allow continued access to the discovered borehole. Resource Environmental was screening and purging fluids from the borehole today. Shallow, monitoring well MW01A has not been drilled yet. A rig is tentatively scheduled for drilling of MW01A and the four deep monitoring wells sometime next week. A puddle within the remediated basin (photo #8) returned a field measured reading of ~360us/cm.Violations of the following remain outstanding against API #015-23892 at this time:25 Pa. Code 78a.56(a), 25 Pa. Code 78a.54, Clean Streams Law 401, and SWMA 301I departed the site at 1030 hours.

Comments: This well was inspected as part of an on going stray gas migration case involving gas migrating into a private water supply (CTS#373559).¿¿ ¿¿ ¿¿ The well head and casing strings were observed at the time of inspection for leaks, deterioration, and possible failures.¿¿ As part of the investigation 1 slam bar hole approximately 1-2 feet from the well head was placed into the ground to identify if any methane was migrating from the well bore.¿¿3% LEL was detected in this slam bar hole. At approximately 11:00 the well was vented and the bubbling could no longer be heard. At approximately 11:36 the methane levels in the annulus dropped to 9% methane by volume. For safety reasons only one slam bar hole was placed in the ground on the windward side of the well bore due to the high amount of methane flowing from the annulus. 3% LEL was detected in this slam bar hole. Code Chapter 78 and ensure that the integrity of the well is maintained and health, safety, environment and property are protected. ¿¿ VIOLATION:78.88(d) - OPERATING WELLS – MECHANICAL INTEGRITY OF OPERATING WELLS - Operator failed to immediately notify the Department and take corrective actions to repair or replace defective equipment or casing for wells exhibiting progressive corrosion, rusting or other signs of equipment deterioration that compromise the integrity of the well. ¿¿ VIOLATION: 78.81(a)1 - CASING AND CEMENTING – GENERAL PROVISIONS - Operator conducted casing and cementing activities that failed to allow for effective control of the well at all times. At this time, the Department is requesting an investigation into the possible source of methane to be conducted by the operator.

Comments: On 10/16/25 Oil and gas inspector Chuck Reaggle conducted a compliance schedule evaluation inspection of the HUMBERSTON UNIT 1H OG Well Permit number 051-24367. An Act 9 sign, Emergency response plan, and erosion and sediment control plans are present at the site entrance. At the time of this inspection, I met with Moody and associates, INC representatives; Project manager Mr. Matt Kapral, and Geoscientist Mr. Joshua Lynch and LPR representative Jim Barnes to observe soil gas readings being taken. Moody and associates took 20 soil readings utilizing their Bascom-Turner EGA-611. Points were every 5' from the well up to 25' to the north, south, east, and west. The results of the soil readings had the highest detection of methane gas from the soils at west 5' @ 22,200 Parts per million at peak. And 540 parts per million sustained. (Noted in picture 14). Moody and associates also took a reading utilizing their Bascom-Turner EGA-611 at the well casing isolated from the surrounding atmosphere and detected 14 Parts per million of carbon monoxide. 78% Methane. 4.8% Oxygen. And 0 Parts per million of hydrogen sulfide. (Noted in picture 8 and 9) Two isotopic samples were also taken from the isolated casing. Moody and associates took soil gas samples from each corner of the well pad. (Seen in pictures 10, 11, 12, 13) Utilizing the departments Bascom-Turner EGA-411, I observed the following readings at the well,27 Parts per million of carbon monoxide. 48% Methane. 15.6% Oxygen. (Noted in picture 3)

Permit API: 015-23753
Unconventional: Yes

Municipality: Terry Twp
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 3/08/2023
Comments: On 3/8/2023, DEP representative John Rogers conducted an Incident - Response to Accident or Event inspection at the Chesapeake Grippo well site. It was 32 degrees and lightly snowing when I arrived on location. On 3/6/2023 Chesapeake personnel identified a water puddle on the unprotected pad surface with elevated conductance on the southwest corner of the pad in the location where chemical ASTs and a freshwater AST were stationed during recent frac operations. No release was reported in this area during the frac or drilling operations. It is expected that an unknown quantity of produced water or brine may have been released during fracking operations. They began excavating the area and had removed 20 truckloads when they contacted the department on 3/7/2023 to report the release. They continued removing material and were still excavating during this inspection. The excavated material was being hauled to the Chesapeake Stoorza well site for temporary storage prior to disposal.I met Creston Envirionmental's Andrew Steffe, who was field testing water and soil from and around the excavation. Andrew reported that he had gotten readings as high as 50 mS conductance from a water puddle that was in the area being excavated. Readings from the soils ranged from 0.1 mS conductance to 6.0 mS conductance. We measured the current extent of the excavation at 162' x 50'. It was approximately 3' deep. A water puddle in the bottom of west end of the excavated area field tested at 15.95 mS conductance. I field tested water in two test pits that were near the north side of the excavated area; water in the east pit was 6.13 mS conductance and the west pit was >20.0 mS conductance. The upper limit of the Oakton PCTS-50 is 20.0 mS conductance. Andrew said that the excavation would continue until he got readings that were under 1.0 mS conductance.I field tested water on the northeast corner of the pad with results at 1.3 mS, 0.5 mS, and 0.5 mS. Drilling mats were being pressure washed on the northwest corner of the pad, the washing being conducted over secondary containment. Water on the east side of the drilling mat wash station field tested at 1.4 mS conductance and on the west side field tested at 0.6 mS conductance. Water in the wash station secondary containment field tested at 1.8 mS conductance.There are five wells on site. Crews were in the process of putting the five wells into production. API/well permit numbers are posted at the entrance to the site. No bubbling within the cellars was observed. The GPUs and production tank were not connected to the wellheads yet.Most of the site appeared stable and well vegetated, meeting the 70% uniform, perennial, vegetative cover. Temporary stabilization was witnessed in some areas. PCSM is addressed on site by three retentive grading/infiltration areas that are adequately stabilized and functioning as designed. Temporary compost filter socks remain in place below the infiltration areasThis spill constitutes violations of these three regulations; 78a 56[a), SWMA 301, and CSL 402(b).The DEP recommends pursuing Act 2 remediation in accordance with 78a 66(c)I left the site at 1145 hrs.

Comments: On 6/2/2026, DEP representative John Rogers conducted a drilling/alteration inspection at the Seneca Resource's Taft 851 well site located in Middlebury Township, Tioga County. It was 60 degrees and clear when I arrived on location. When I arrived at the active north pad, I met with Seneca's Mark McCormick who described current operations as follows: Evolution Well Services has been on site since 2/13/2026, performing stimulation operations on eight recently drilled gas wells. The crew was currently alternating between the 70HU, 204HU, 203HU, and had just finished the 72HU on 6/1/2026. The crew has completed the stages on the other four wells. Mark expects stimulation activities on the eight wells to be completed by 6/9/2026.Stimulation operations were being conducted within secondary containment. There were 32 frac tanks stationed in secondary containment on the west side of the pad, four for freshwater and 28 for produced water. Additionally, there were four pump down frac tanks, two gas buster frac tanks and five working frac tanks staged in secondary containment on the pad. Chemical tanks and totes were staged in secondary containment.Five wells have been completed at the site and were staged for production. Two produced water tanks and five GPUs that are connected to the completed wells were stationed in secondary containment.Three sediment traps and one sediment basin have been installed on site and along the access road. They have not been converted to PCSM BMPs yet. Sediment trap 3 and the sediment basin did have standing water. Temporary compost filter socks remain installed throughout the site. The original south pad and access road for the Taft 851 1V well have been returned to original grade, the well pad and associated diversion berms were adequately stabilized. Separate construction projects are underway, installing water and gas pipelines on the south side of the pad.During the inspection, I field screened the following for conductivity: A 2' x 3' puddle of water above the center outfall from the north side of the pad, tested at 7.81 mS conductance. Liquid flowing from the center north outfall into the basin tested at 8.08 mS conductance. Liquid in the basin near the northeast outfall tested at 4.04 mS conductance. I met Seneca's Jeff Passerrello on location during the inspection. He was collecting water samples from the location. I discussed my findings with him.Violations are still outstanding for inspection ID 3846665 and ID 3855651 for puddles of water with elevated conductance discovered on the pad surface and in the sediment basin during completion operations. The DEP recommends that Seneca continues to monitor the conditions on the pad surface and the sediment basin and remove elevated conductance fluids and soils as discovered. Prevent elevated conductance fluids from leaving the facility and causing pollution to the waters of the Commonwealth. I left the site at 1200 hours.

Comments: The Department received a complaint with concerns about the secondary containment around a pair of 500 bbl tanks that are plumbed to the Brown 1 well. These tanks are located along Farm Lane, in Pleasant Township. The complainant was concerned that if a release occurred the gravel and unconsolidated material in the containment would not be sufficient to contain a release.The small upper containment directly around the stock tanks is constructed with a dirt and gravel base and walls, and includes a drain pipe that is directed the into a second containment downslope of the upper containment. The upper containment wall and base material around the tanks consists of gravel and does not appear to comply with the permeability requirements. In its current state the height of the upper containment wall would not be sufficient in containing a substantial release. The lower containment at the bottom of the slope, intended to contain an overflow from the upper containment in the event of a substantial release, is nearly full of water and does not have the capacity required by Chapter 78.64.

Violation Code: 78.86 - CASING AND CEMENTING - DEFECTIVE CASING OR CEMENTING - Operator failed to report defect in a well that has defective, insufficient or improperly cemented casing to the Department within 24 hours of discovery. Operator failed to correct defect or failed to submit a plan to correct the defect for approval by the Department within 30 days.
Violation ID: 880697
Permit API: 131-20278
Unconventional: Yes
County: Wyoming
Municipality: Windham Twp
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 2020-03-13
Comments: At time of inspection, 40 degs. and cloudy. There are (5) wells on this pad. They are the Jack 1H, 2H, 3H, 4H and the 5H, all were in production. The (9x5) and the (13x9) annulus vents are plumbed to surface w/2" pipe and T'd into a 2" common pipe venting to the prod. tanks with the exception of the 2H, which is a (2) string well and only has the (9x5) annulus venting to tanks, the (20x9) annulus has an open annulus. All annulus vents are open and venting to production tanks. The cellars had water in them w/ no bubbling observed during insp.. - The Operators well tender (Giovanni Dicupillo) was on site today to isolate the (13x9) annuli of the 1H, 3H and the 4H due to gas being detected in previous inspections. An ALTAIR 5X gas meter (cal. 3/4/20) was turned on to screen for gas at the isolated annuli and left on to check for gas at cellars, at the well heads and left on during walk around pad and prod. equipment. No gas was detected at any of the isolated (13x9) annuli or in the ambient air. - The Jack 1H was shut in at time of inspection due to maintenance being performed on GPU by Operator. - Individual well pressures listed below were all taken off SCADA gauges: - 1H - prod. tree top press.: 1,121 psi., prod. csg. press.: 550.0 psi., (9x5) annulus press.: 2.3 psi, (13x9) annulus press.: 2.3 psi., and prod. line press.: 2.7 psi. (OUTST) - 4H - prod. tree top press.: 973.9 psi., prod. csg. press.: 1,012.2 psi., (9x5) annulus press.: 1 psi, (13x9) annulus press.: 0.0 psi., and prod. line press.: 971.0 psi. (OUTST) - 5H - prod. tree top press.: 973.1 psi., prod. csg. press.: 103.4 psi., (9x5) annulus press.: 2.0 psi, (13x9) annulus press.: 1 psi., and prod. line press.: 970 psi. - There is self contained ancillary equipment on site. - No obvious concerns or new violations noted.
